title: Polynomial quotient algebra maps are evaluations at roots
statement:
Let $R$ and $C$ be commutative rings, let $\rho:R\to C$ give $C$ its $R$-algebra structure [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and let $f\in R[t]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Put $B=R[t]/(f)$ with quotient map $q$ and $\alpha=q(t)$. For $g=\sum_i r_it^i$, write $g_\rho(c)=\sum_i\rho(r_i)c^i$, a finite sum. The map
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{R\text{-alg}}(B,C)\longrightarrow\{c\in C:f_\rho(c)=0\},\qquad\varphi\longmapsto\varphi(\alpha)$$
is bijective. Its inverse sends $c$ to the unique $R$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi_c$ satisfying
$$\varphi_c(q(g))=g_\rho(c)\quad(g\in R[t]).$$
In particular the finite-sum evaluation is independent of the representative of the class $q(g)$.
